title: The store's sealed-words check scans the model-4 sets in minutes, not hours
request: The owner: every agent's thinking kept for training; the store rebuild after adding reasoning took over an hour on the model-4 conversation sets.
spec: Keep the contamination check's result the same (a sealed person's words or a benchmark task keep an example out of train and dev) and make it fast.
plan: Measure where the build spends its time.
Replace the slow part, keep the behaviour, test.

decisions.decision: Plain substring checks for the sealed sentences, and a memo of texts already checked.
decisions.why: One regex of 1,897 alternatives took 132 ms per 10 KB of text; substrings take 9 ms, and a system prompt or tool list repeats in thousands of examples.

findings.defect: The model-4 build step ran for about 45 minutes with no output.
findings.scenario: After every example began carrying its thinking text, the store rebuild sat on model 4 at one CPU, writing nothing.
findings.cause: Every text of every example was matched against one regular expression of 1,897 sealed sentences: 132 ms per 10 KB.
findings.fix: Substring checks (9 ms per 10 KB) and a memo keyed by the text, so a repeated system prompt is checked once.
findings.test: tests/test_store_sets_llm.py (the sealed and benchmark cases still kept out)

measurements.name: Contamination check per 10 KB of text
measurements.result: 132 ms with the regex, 9.4 ms with substrings, before the memo
limits: a synthetic 10 KB text; the build's own time is measured on its next run

outcome: Adding thinking to every example no longer makes the store's rebuild take hours.
lessons: When examples grow (here, by their thinking), every per-text check grows with them: measure the slowest step before guessing.
risks: The memo is cleared at 200,000 texts; memory stays bounded.
